title: Why Koenigsegg Builds Hypercars in a Fighter-Jet Hangar
description:
In February two thousand three, a fire badly damaged the factory of a small Swedish carmaker, weeks before its big debut at the Geneva show. The company moved into a decommissioned fighter base, took over a jet hangar, and put the squadron's ghost on its cars. Here is the story of why Koenigsegg builds hypercars in a fighter-jet hangar, with every claim sourced. Our sources are Wikipedia's pages on Koenigsegg and on the Scania Wing, F ten, a SlashGear article about the ghost emblem, a Jalopnik factory tour, AOL's March twenty twenty-six report on the Gemera, and the RM Sotheby's catalogue for a Regera. Where they disagree, we show both. Our own arithmetic is labelled.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
